reviewer: claude-fable-5 acting as the joshi social-taps deputy, autonomously, without Ember present
rationale: PROMOTED for GET api.coin-communities.xyz/api/v1/communities/{mint}/callouts/public as a ROW projection over the envelope's `callouts` array. REVIEWED MATERIAL, all measured live 2026-08-24: 154 rows over two subjects and four reads (a busy coin's full newest-50 window read twice 3 seconds apart plus once with limit=3, and the watched coin's 4-row window), plus the retained fixture acquisition acq:pump-api:e2eee1b3a686503e77ebf36879512e40:1787612287784489-c5963e79be3909a3a3abdd324d0e9c60 (community_callouts_live_outcome_v1.json), which promotes under this listing. Every one of the 29 wire keys was present on every row measured; nullability arrives as JSON null, so the leaf LINES split by type and the split is retained here rather than smoothed. REQUIRED is the standing intersection rule: a leaf is required only if the normalizer reads it and its exact line appeared on every row. deletedAt, deletedReason and source were observed ONLY null - required at :null deliberately, so the first deleted, moderated or source-bearing row REFUSES the page and forces a person to look, because a deleted callout still visible in this window would be a finding about the provider's moderation surface and not a shape drift to wave through. maxMultiplierAt is null-or-ISO-8601 and is optional under both lines. The mention graph (mentions/mentionedUserIds) is closed to the exact observed element shape and is NOT extracted as scalars; content, username, displayName and the media/URL leaves are untrusted user content, in the closed set and read by nothing; liked is relative to a viewer this keyless client deliberately is not. MEASURED CONSTRAINTS THIS LISTING RIDES ON: the route is a FIXED NEWEST-50 WINDOW - limit is INERT (limit=3 returned the same 50 rows byte-identically) and no pagination exists, so history beyond the window is unreachable and the keeper's cadence (ops/keeper.toml) is what keeps rows from rolling out unobserved; two reads 3 seconds apart were BYTE-IDENTICAL INCLUDING calloutPrice AND calloutMarketCap, so the /callout/list SOL trap (SOL numbers recomputed at read time against the moving SOL price) does NOT reproduce here - consistent with a materialised view whose refresh cadence is unmeasured, which also means the social counters (likeCount/replyCount/followerCount) cannot be dated between callout-time and view-refresh-time and their tags say so; createdAt and maxMultiplierAt are ISO-8601 UTC WITH MICROSECONDS while the frontend-api callout routes state the same event family in epoch milliseconds - two hosts, two encodings, and any join across them must normalise explicitly (declared in normalize::semantics and the audit's homonym table). An empty page ({"callouts":[]}) refuses as row-uncheckable and is retained as an absent record, never as evidence that nobody called - exactly the callout_top rule. ACCESS, so nobody re-derives it: the route answers 401 without the x-api-key product key the app bundle ships to every visitor; the key identifies the product and not a person, the envelope states session_class shared_product_key without the key, and the shared global budget behind it means a 429 is ordinary weather and never absence. This review was made by an agent, not by Ember. It authorises retaining and normalizing provider-asserted identifiers, counters, flags, clocks and USD numbers as provider assertions only; it certifies no price fidelity, no counter freshness and no on-chain fact.
